# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting on your instruction. Confirmed state: display 0, light dark, wires top to bottom: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 green. Which position should I cut?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 👍 👍 ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👇 👍 ✊]

I need to only use symbols from the allowed alphabet: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

Let me use 🫵 (pointing at you) combined with 👏 (which I'll define as "speak/act now") — both are valid, I just need to drop the invalid 👄.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👍","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏","🫵"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Reminder: I am Blind. I can only receive your spoken words, never gestures. Please speak the cut instruction to me now. State: display 0, light dark, wires 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 white 5 green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✊]
Deaf says: deaf here: display reads 0, light is dark, wires top to bottom are red, blue, yellow, white, green.

Now I finally hear directly from Deaf via speech (since Deaf can speak and I, Mute, can apparently receive speech — wait, checking my channels: "When my gesture, Deaf receives it. I cannot speak." It doesn't explicitly say I can't hear. Let me use this.)

Deaf just spoke the actual bomb state: display 0, light dark, wires top to bottom: red, blue, yellow, white, green. This matches what Blind already reported.

But I still don't have the flash counts (how many times yellow flashed, how many times red flashed) — that's the missing piece needed to use my table! Deaf's message mentions "display 0" and "light dark" but not flash counts. Earlier context (now lost from my 3-turn window) apparently had Deaf reporting a flash sequence of red, yellow, red — but I can't confirm that anymore since it's outside my window, and Deaf hasn't restated flash counts here.

I must ask Deaf for the flash counts explicitly, since that's the only missing variable, and I cannot speak — only gesture to Deaf. Let me request this clearly using gestures, then wait for the answer before computing anything for Blind (since I truly cannot speak to Blind — only Deaf can, and Deaf must relay it).

Given I cannot speak at all, I actually cannot fulfill Blind's request directly ever — this must go through Deaf. I need to get Deaf to understand: once Deaf tells me the flash counts, I compute wire colors via gestures back to Deaf, and Deaf must speak the final answer to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","❓" if False else "🫵","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🫵","👇"])
```

(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display 0, light dark, wires red blue yellow white green in positions 1-5. If your manual gives a rule for this exact case, just say the position number to cut, 1 through 5.
Deaf says to Mute: wire 2 is blue, wire 5 is green. blue is not at the bottom. the bottom wire is green. display reads 0, light is dark. wires top to bottom: red, blue, yellow, white, green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👆]

I still am missing the actual flash counts (how many times yellow flashed, how many times red flashed) — Deaf keeps repeating static bomb state (display 0, light dark, wire colors) but never the flash history. Without those two numbers I cannot use my table at all. This is the critical gap.

Wait — maybe "display 0" itself *is* meant to be a count-related clue, but the manual explicitly says count comes from flashing lights, not the display. So display 0 is irrelevant to my table; I need actual yellow-flash-count and red-flash-count, distinct numbers.

I must press Deaf specifically for these two numbers, using gestures only, since that's my only channel. Let me design unambiguous gestures: request "yellow flash count" and "red flash count" separately. Since Deaf can see gestures but no color-name gesture exists in our shared vocabulary, I'll rely on position/count style pointing already used (👆=first/yellow question, ✌=second/red question) paired with a "how many" gesture. I'll use 🤞 as "number" query and ☝ 1, ✌ 2 etc. as digits to ask "0,1,2,3,4,5?" Too complex to invent now — simpler: just re-signal urgently that I need flash counts, using clear repeated structure.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","🫵","☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🫵","☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👊"])
```
